correctness.summary: The complete-randomization error is exactly a scaled simple-random-sample mean of bounded scores. Serfling's finite-population Hoeffding bound gives the upper tail. A binary sharp-null endpoint population makes the error hypergeometric, and Stirling expansion of an exact point mass matches the quadratic exponent. Independent stratum mgfs and a quadratic allocation of hypergeometric deviations yield the matching stratified constant. Algebraic factors and numerical exact-probability checks were rechecked.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Sampling-without-replacement concentration, finite-population moderate deviations, and the without-replacement SATE representation are prior art. Recent randomized-experiment papers establish finite-sample intervals, optimal rates, and sharp mean-squared minimax risk, but the sources inspected did not state the exact worst-case moderate-deviation exponent for the standard difference-in-means estimator or the stratified harmonic constant. The main residual risk is older survey-sampling or permutation-test literature containing an equivalent theorem under different terminology.

value.summary: The result identifies the exact bounded-outcome logarithmic tail constant behind recent rate-level finite-sample inference, supplies matching finite Serfling confidence bounds, and gives a sharp stratified allocation law showing how heterogeneous treatment fractions affect worst-case concentration.

limitations: Treatment fractions must converge to interior values for the sharp asymptotic theorem.
The number of strata is fixed.
The moderate-deviation sequence satisfies nt_n^2/log n tending to infinity.
Studentized, variance-adaptive, and alternative estimators are not covered.
The theorem fixes the assignment design and difference-in-means estimator and is not minimax over all procedures.
Older survey-sampling and permutation-test literature remains a residual originality risk.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
